[Question 9(a)]  
10. At about 1457 hours, I directed crew members to lay fire hoses and deploy 2 water jets for firefighting towards the lower portion of scaffolding structures at the exterior of Wang Cheong House facing Island House Lane. I observed that the fire was vertically spreading upward along the scaffolding structure rapidly. A large quantity of burning bamboo, wooden planks, and miscellaneous articles were falling from height of Wang Cheong House to the open ground on ground floor. These burning articles piled up and blocked the rear exit of Wang Cheong House facing Island House Lane. I also noted the fire spread from the rear re-entrant of Wang Cheong House facing Island House Lane to its south-east side.

11. At about 1459 hours, I returned to the roundabout outside Wang Cheong House. I noted the fire had already spread from the rear façade of Wang Cheong House facing Island House Lane to its west façade via flying embers. At the same time, I also noted that the open ground near the front entrance of Wang Cheong House was well alight. Certain burning materials, including flames and other indistinguishable combustibles, were carried by the wind from the direction of Wang Cheong House to Wang Tai House. At 1500 hours, I noted that the fire spread from Wang Cheong House to Wang Tai House (the east façade) (Layout Plan (3) refers).
